# Artifact Keeper 1.11.2

A reliability, audit and detection patch release on the 1.11 line: 50 changelog entries from 52 pull requests since 1.11.1. The headline is **a database outage now answers a retryable `503` with `Retry-After: 1` instead of `401` or `500`** (#4750, #4756, #4765), so Docker, twine, cargo, npm and CI runners retry through a database blip instead of aborting or asking for a login. Around it are one security fix (plugin reload now runs the outbound-URL check before re-cloning, #4757, GHSA-r8fc-5fvw-rvh4), a lockstep move of the bundled trivy and the trivy server sidecar to 0.76.0 that **operators who run their own trivy server must follow** (#4712), audit rows for every request now carrying the client IP and many previously unaudited admin actions now writing audit rows (#4762, #4710, #4709), new detection metrics and log fields (#4676, #4677, #4674), and 33 fixes across proxy caching, migration, replication, Maven, npm, Conan, conda and SSO. **No schema migrations.** Four new settings: `LOG_ANSI`, `PLUGINS_ENABLED`, `DATABASE_TCP_KEEPALIVES` and `HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG`; `PLUGINS_ENABLED` and `HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG` keep the previous behaviour by default, while `LOG_ANSI` defaults to `auto` (no colour codes in non-terminal logs) and `DATABASE_TCP_KEEPALIVES` is on by default.

## Read this first: what now answers with an error or refuses

- **Scanning stops unless a self-run trivy server moves to 0.76.0 together with the backend** (#4712). The scanner adapter's bundled trivy and the trivy server sidecar move together from 0.74.0 to 0.76.0, published as scanner-adapter 1.5.0. In client/server mode (`SCANNER_TRIVY_SERVER`) the adapter refuses to scan unless the server reports the same trivy release as its bundled client: `/probe/ready` stays `503` and every scan fails closed with "client/server mode needs matching releases". The stock `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.local-dev.yml` and `docker-compose.test.yml` now run `ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy:0.76.0`, and the Helm chart's `trivy.image.tag` moves in artifact-keeper-iac. **A deployment that pins its own trivy server image, or points the adapter at an external one, has to move that pin to 0.76.0 when it takes this release.** Client/server mode now carries cryptographic assets and modular-package details over the RPC, so modular packages on RHEL-family targets, which client/server mode used to skip silently, are now detected as in standalone mode.
- **A database outage answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1`, not `401` or `500`.** During credential checks (#4750): a closed pool, a lost or refused connection, a statement or lock timeout or a server shutting down used to return `401 "Invalid or expired token"` from the auth middleware, and every such failure on `/v2`, `/v2/` and `/v2/token` returned `401`; they now return `503` on the auth middleware, the format-endpoint resolver and every `/v2` verb. During login and other handlers (#4756): `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and any handler whose own query hits the outage return `503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of `500 DATABASE_ERROR`. A pool-acquire timeout still returns `503 POOL_EXHAUSTED`. On the format endpoints (#4765): npm, OCI, Git LFS and protobuf Connect answer `503` in their own error shapes (npm `{"error": ...}`, Git LFS `{"message": ...}`, OCI `UNAVAILABLE`, Connect `unavailable`), and OCI and Connect also use those codes now for a saturated pool, which said `INTERNAL_ERROR` / `internal` before. An unknown, wrong, expired or revoked credential still returns `401`, and query or data errors still return `500`. Alerting that counted `401`s or `500`s during an outage will see `503`s instead.
- **Reloading a git-sourced WASM plugin validates its stored source first: `400`** (#4757, GHSA-r8fc-5fvw-rvh4). `POST /api/v1/plugins/{id}/reload` re-cloned the stored `source_url` with no SSRF validation. Every git re-fetch now runs the same outbound-URL check install does and refuses a blocked source with the same `400`, naming `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` for an address an operator can admit, before any clone is attempted. Reload is admin-only. A plugin whose source now resolves to a private address and that you mean to keep reloading needs that address in `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS`.
- **A Remote whose upstream promises a `Content-Length` and sends no body answers `502 UPSTREAM_SHORT_BODY`** (#4759), naming the repository and the expected and received byte counts (or serving the stale cached copy when stale-if-error has one), instead of dropping the client connection with no status. The streaming path now waits for the first body byte before it answers. A body that ends short after bytes were forwarded still closes the connection, now with a warn naming the cache key.
- **An IdP that answers the token request without an `id_token` gets `502 OIDC_NO_ID_TOKEN`** (#4699) naming the provider (and the IdP's OAuth `error` code when sent), instead of `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`.
- **Smaller refusals.** A `PUT /{pkg}/-rev/{rev}` that removes no npm version is refused with `400`, so other packument edits sent there (such as `npm owner`) fail visibly; npm unpublish is refused with `405` on Remote and `400` on virtual repositories (#4025). An npm version whose metadata contains a NUL character is rejected with `400` instead of being stored without its metadata (#4643). A Git LFS upload whose declared `Content-Length` exceeds `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` is refused before the body is read (#4595). An OCI chunked-upload commit whose stored part does not match the length recorded at PATCH time is a `500` naming the part instead of `DIGEST_INVALID` (#4646). Clearing a repository's project with `{"project_id": null}` from a repository-level admin alone gets `403` (#4026).

## Read this second: behaviour that changes without an error

- **Every audit row written while handling a request now records the client IP** (#4762), including `REPOSITORY_CREATED`, `USER_CREATED`, role, password, TOTP, token, settings and policy changes, which stored an empty `ip_address` (and a `null` `source_ip` in the audit stream) before. The address is the request's verified client IP, the same one login records: the TCP peer, or the forwarded address only behind a trusted proxy with `XFF_TRUSTED_FOR_AUTHZ=true`. Background-job rows, and requests behind a trusted proxy without that setting, still record no IP.
- **Collected logs lose their ANSI colour codes by default** (#4674). The new `LOG_ANSI` (`auto`, `true`, `false`) defaults to `auto`: colour only when stdout is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset, so container and systemd logs are plain and Loki or SIEM filters on `uri=`, `status=` or `correlation_id=` start matching. `LOG_ANSI=true` restores the previous output. `LOG_FORMAT=json` lines logged during a request gain top-level `method`, `uri`, `correlation_id` and `http.route`, and the `Request completed` line adds `status`, `user` (omitted when anonymous), `ip` and `latency_ms`; existing keys are unchanged. The text format's `Request completed` line also records `user`, `ip` and `latency_ms`. `LOG_FORMAT` accepts `text` as the default format's name (`pretty` still works). Field reference: `docs/operations/logging.md`.
- **OCI requests in the `ak_http_*` series are labelled with route templates** (#4676). They were all `path="unmatched"`; they now carry the spec's template, such as `/v2/{name}/manifests/{reference}`. Dashboards that filtered on `unmatched` to find registry traffic need the new labels.
- **A trusted gateway's `X-Request-ID` becomes the correlation ID** (#4677): up to 128 visible ASCII characters from a peer in `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, after an explicit `X-Correlation-ID` and before `traceparent`. From any other peer it is ignored as before.
- **The OIDC `redirect_uri` behind a reverse proxy follows only trusted forwarding headers** (#4143). With `AK_EXTERNAL_URL` unset and `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` set, `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `X-Forwarded-Host` are honoured only from a listed proxy; with the list empty the previous behaviour is kept. An `http://` `redirect_uri` (which Microsoft Entra rejects with AADSTS50011) now logs a warning naming `AK_EXTERNAL_URL`, the setting that fixes it.
- **The OIDC authorization-code exchange sends the provider's configured scopes on the token request** (#4699), default `openid profile email`, which Microsoft Entra's v2 token endpoint needs to return an `id_token`.
- **Conan files on S3, GCS or Azure are written under repository-scoped keys** (#4694): new recipe and package files go to `conan/{repository_id}/...`, so the same revision can be uploaded to more than one Conan repository instead of being refused with `409 ... refusing cross-repository overwrite`. Existing files stay where they are and keep serving from the key their artifact row records; filesystem storage and `STORAGE_KEY_SCHEME=flat` keep the flat key.
- **A Maven version's catalog size is the total of its files** (#4633), not whichever file had the smallest checksum. The Packages list, package detail and Versions tab show the new value; quotas and storage totals are unaffected. Existing versions are corrected by the next upload into the version, or at once by `POST /api/v1/admin/packages/backfill`, which records the same total for Maven and Gradle.
- **A grant on a virtual repository still does not grant its members, and the REST listings now say so** (#4690). `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/members` and `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/artifacts` add an `X-AK-Virtual-Members-Notice` header when the caller can read no member. Format routes still answer `404`. `docs/repository-visibility.md` documents the rule with a group-grant example.
- **Audit retention now runs on a schedule, and an unsaved period deletes nothing** (#4718). An hourly job deletes rows older than `audit_retention_days`, in batches of 5,000, on one replica at a time. `0`, or a period that was never saved, leaves retention off, and `GET /api/v1/admin/settings` reports `audit_retention_days: 0` in that case instead of a `90` that was never applied, so upgrading deletes no audit rows. `POST /api/v1/admin/cleanup` with the period at `0` or unsaved now deletes no audit rows; at `0` it used to delete all of them.
- **Postgres connections arm server-side TCP keepalives and startup retries the initial connect** (#4549). Every pool and single-flight lock connection sets `tcp_keepalives_idle=15`, `tcp_keepalives_interval=5` and `tcp_keepalives_count=3`, so a force-killed pod's sessions are reaped in about 30 s instead of about 2 h; `DATABASE_TCP_KEEPALIVES=false` turns this off (for example behind a pooler in transaction mode). Startup retries the first connect up to five times with backoff, and a database that stays down fails the process in about 40 s with the defaults. `.env.example` now documents the connection budget, whose shipped defaults (3 × 50 = 150) exceed a stock server's 100 `max_connections`.
- **The setup gate and the startup password regeneration concern only the built-in `admin`** (#4634). Another admin with a pending password change no longer arms the gate (which made every route answer `403 SETUP_REQUIRED`) or gets `admin`'s password overwritten on restart. If `admin` has been renamed or removed and another local admin exists, boot creates and arms nothing.
- **Smaller changes.** Git LFS uploads follow `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` (10 GiB by default, `0` for no limit) instead of a fixed 2 GB (#4595). `PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` with `{"project_id": null}` now clears the project, and the `REPOSITORY_UPDATED` row records `project_change` (#4026). `npm unpublish` now removes the version or package, needing the `delete:artifacts` scope and the repository `delete` action (#4025). LDAP login and the SSO exchange now return `expires_in` and size the access cookie to the token's real lifetime (#4648). Hosted npm packages and Go modules, and re-uploads to the same path, now reach push and mirror peers (#4643, #4658). Remote and virtual conda channels serve real `current_repodata.json`, `run_exports.json` and `repodata.json.sig`, and `patch_instructions.json` on hosted and virtual channels answers `404` instead of an empty `200` (#4708). RubyGems indices list hyphen-digit gem names such as `qa-gem-2` correctly (#4645). Debian and Maven repositories migrated from Artifactory or Nexus now register their packages; repositories migrated earlier are repaired by re-running the job (Debian) or by the catalog backfill (Maven) (#4657, #4691). `PLUGINS_ENABLED=false` disables the WASM plugin runtime and leaves its routes unregistered; the default is enabled (#4650). `HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG` sets the API listener's accept queue; unset keeps the OS maximum, and the granted backlog is logged at startup (#4647).

## Read this third: hardening and detection

- **New metrics** (#4676, #4677, #4642, #4711, #4549). `ak_http_connections_open`, `ak_rate_limit_rejections_total{limiter}`, `ak_ssrf_blocks_total{surface}`, `ak_auth_failures_total{surface,reason}` (reason bucketed, never a username or token) and `ak_proxy_scan_verdicts_total{verdict,action}` (#4676); `ak_permission_condition_evaluations_total{condition,outcome}` (#4677); `ak_artifact_uploads_total`, `ak_artifact_upload_size_bytes` and `ak_artifact_downloads_total`, which were defined but never recorded (#4642); `ak_conda_attestation_total`, `ak_conda_install_script_findings_total` and `ak_conda_allowlist_dropped_total`, labelled by repository key and never by package name (#4711); `ak_db_pool_connection_failures_total{stage}` (#4549). Scheduled Remote cache evictions now count toward `ak_cleanup_items_removed_total{type="lifecycle"}` (#4451). Counters restart from zero with the process; query them with `increase()`.
- **New audit events.** `LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED` for a login refused `429` by the login limiters, at most once per source IP per limiter window, and `EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_INGESTED` for `POST /api/v1/security/findings/external` (#4677). Quarantine, promotion approval and promotion, permission rule, SSO provider, signing-key, webhook and sync-policy changes (#4710). Conda publishes, withdrawals, attestation outcomes and environment registrations and deletions (#4709). `REPOSITORY_UPDATED` on `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/upstream-auth`, recording the auth-type change and a `credentials_changed` flag (#4529). No row carries a secret.
- **New and updated documentation.** `docs/operations/detection-signals.md` (#4677), `docs/operations/detection-metrics.md` (#4676), `docs/operations/logging.md` (#4674), `docs/operations/artifact-metrics.md` (#4642), `docs/operations/conda-security-metrics.md` (#4711), `docs/operations/load-shedding.md` with sizing guidance for CPU-limited replicas (#4647), `docs/proxy-cache-freshness.md` on the yank asymmetry (#4028), and the action and `details` reference in `docs/audit-events.md` (#4709, #4710, #4762).
- **Proxy-cache integrity.** A publish that lands a zero-byte or truncated object writes no sidecar and drops the object, and entries already poisoned that way become a cache miss and heal on the next request (#4630). On filesystem storage, where sidecars pin no ETag, a body whose size disagrees with its sidecar is evicted and refetched instead of being served as `Content-Length: N` over a short body (#4758). A failed final filesystem write now returns an error instead of publishing a short object (#4646). A warm npm Remote tarball is served without reading the packument (#4692).
- **Clearer private-network refusals.** Refusing an LDAP server, identity provider, upstream or webhook on an RFC 1918, CGNAT or IPv6 unique-local address now names `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` with the refused address as the example (#4638). Cloud metadata, loopback and link-local addresses stay refused even when a containing range is listed.

## Dependency updates

- `object_store` 0.14.2 (#2158), which backs S3 storage, depends on quick-xml ^0.41, so the vulnerable quick-xml 0.39.2 it pulled in leaves the graph and the two `.cargo/audit.toml` ignores for RUSTSEC-2026-0194/0195 are removed. The upgrade also drops the second reqwest (0.12). S3 TLS trust rules are unchanged. SigV4 signing failures on the AWS upstream-auth and S3 REST fallback paths now return an error instead of panicking.
- The backend image's bundled `grype` moves from v0.118.0 to **v0.120.1** (#3698), which pins `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.57.0 (past CVE-2026-56855 and CVE-2026-78662, `x/crypto/ssh` denial of service) and `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.83.2 itself. The build now fails if the binary records `x/crypto` below v0.56.0, the gRPC override from #3655 and #3790 is deleted, and the `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 override for CVE-2026-78669 stays. `grype --version` prints `0.120.1`.
- scanner-adapter 1.5.0 bundles `artifact-keeper/trivy` 0.76.0-r1, upstream v0.76.0 on go1.27.2 with no dependency overrides, because 0.76.0 already pins grpc v1.84.0, `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 and containerd v2.4.1 (#4712). See the first section for the trivy server pairing.
- Dependabot group bumps: the cargo minor/patch group (`serde_json` 1.0.154, `zeroize` 1.9.1, `http-body` 1.1.0, `uuid` 1.28.0, `tokio-util` 0.7.20, `redis` 1.7.1, `hyper` 1.12.0, `zstd` 0.14.2, `sigstore_protobuf_specs` 0.5.2; #4689) and the GitHub Actions group (`actions/download-artifact` 8.0.2, `actions/setup-node` 7.1.0, `github/codeql-action` 4.38.3, `azure/setup-kubectl` 5.2.0; #4748).

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.2]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.2/CHANGELOG.md).
